{{Short description|Cryptanalytic attacks using a system of multivariate equations}}
'''Algebraic attack''' is a method of algebraic [[cryptanalysis]] by which a set of algebraic equations can be used to solve a cryptographic Boolean function that has a low degree or a high degree of [[Non-linear equation|non linearity]]. The main objective is to reduce the non linearity of the equations and then solve the cipher to decrypt into plaintext. It has been used for vulnerability testing for [[encryption]] algorithms as well as hacking systems for malicious intent.

== Theory ==
Algebraic attacks can be used for a variety of [[Cryptosystem|cryptosystems]] which is the encryption scheme consisting of five tuples which are<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last=Kreuzer |first=Martin |date=January 2009 |title=Algebraic Attacks Galore! |url=https://www.degruyterbrill.com:443/document/doi/10.1515/GCC.2009.231/html |journal=Groups – Complexity – Cryptology |volume=1 |issue=2 |doi=10.1515/gcc.2009.231 |issn=1867-1144}}</ref>

* Set of plaintext units denoted as <math>\mathcal{P}</math>
* Set of [[ciphertext]] units denoted as <math>\mathcal{C}</math>
* Set called key space denoted as <math>\mathcal{K}</math>
* Encryption function for every <math>k \in K</math> where <math>E_k : \mathcal{P} \rightarrow \mathcal{C}</math>
* Decryption function for every <math>k \in K</math> where <math>D_k : \mathcal{C} \rightarrow \mathcal{P}</math>

A map between <math>E_{k(1)}</math> and <math display="inline">D_{k(2)}</math>  exists such that <math>E_{k(1)} \circ D_{k(2)} = id_k</math> for every <math>k \in K</math>. Thus the pair <math>(k(1), k(2))</math> becomes [[key pair]].

The most basic process of describing encryption and [[decryption]] in [[cryptography]] using [[XOR cipher]] is as follows with an example :

* <math>\mathcal{P}</math> (10011) [[Exclusive or|XOR]] <math>\mathcal{K}</math> (10110) = <math>\mathcal{C}</math> (00101)
* <math>\mathcal{C}</math> (00101) XOR <math>\mathcal{K}</math> (10110) = <math>\mathcal{P}</math> (10011)

[[File:Public key encryption.svg|thumb|Public key cryptosystem]]
The cryptosystem becomes [[Symmetric-key algorithm|symmetric]] when <math>k(2)</math> can be computed efficiently from <math>E_{k(1)}</math> and <math>k</math> else if not then it is a [[Public-key cryptography|public key]] cryptosystem. In [[block cipher]], the plaintext is broken into plaintext units and encrypted by fixed key <math>k</math> meanwhile in [[stream cipher]], a Boolean function is used to generate a set of keys or keystream <math>k_1, k_2, \ldots</math> from an initial key <math>k</math> and then this keystream is used to encrypt the plaintext units individually.<ref name=":2" />

Assuming <math>\mathcal{P}</math> and <math>\mathcal{C}</math> as subsets of finite vector spaces of characteristic 2 where the field is <math>K = F_q</math> and <math>q = 2^e</math> or <math>p^e</math> where <math>p</math> is the characteristic and

every map <math>\phi : K^n \rightarrow K^m</math> is a polynomial such that

<math>\phi(a_1,\ldots, a_n) = (f_1(a_1,\ldots, a_n), \ldots, f_m(a_1,\ldots, a_n))</math>

The main criteria for deciding to algebraic attack a [[Stream cipher|stream]] or a [[block cipher]] is algebraic immunity <math>AI</math>.

For a set of all Boolean functions <math>B_n</math> of n input variables with mapping of strings to values as <math>\{0, 1\}^n \rightarrow {0, 1}</math> then each Boolean function <math>f</math> can be represented as a multivariate polynomial over [[GF(2)]] which is called the [[algebraic normal form]] (ANF).<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last1=Dalai |first1=Deepak Kumar |last2=Maitra |first2=Subhamoy |date=March 2009 |title=Algebraic Immunity of Boolean Functions - Analysis and Construction |url=http://www.scielo.org.mx/scielo.php?script=sci_abstract&pid=S1405-55462009000100005&lng=es&nrm=iso&tlng=en |journal=[[Computación y Sistemas]] |language=en |volume=12 |issue=3 |pages=297–321 |issn=1405-5546}}</ref>

<math>f(x_1, \ldots, x_n) = a_0 + \sum_{1 \leqslant i \leqslant n} a_i x_i + \sum_{1 \leqslant i \leqslant j \leqslant n} a_{i,j} x_i x_j +\ldots + a_{1,2,\ldots,n} x_1 x_2 \ldots x_n ,</math>

where the coefficients <math>a_0, a_i, a_{i, j} , \ldots, a_{1,2,\ldots,n} \in \{0, 1\}</math> and <math>deg(f)</math> is the algebraic degree or number of variables in highest order term with non zero coefficient.

Also <math>g \in B_n</math> is [[Annihilator method|annihilator]] of <math>f \in B_n</math> if <math>f \cdot g = 0</math>

Given <math>f \in B_n</math>, algebraic immunity <math>AI(f)</math> is defined as minimum degree of all annihilators of <math>f</math> or <math>1 + f</math>.<ref name=":3" />

<math>AI(f) = (f \oplus 1) \cdot g = 0</math>

This annihilator is exactly located at <math>\left \lceil \frac{N}{2} \right \rceil</math> therefore,<ref name=":3" />

<math>AI(f) \leqslant \left \lceil \frac{N}{2} \right \rceil</math>

== History of algorithms and preventive techniques ==

=== Early algorithms ===
Algebraic attack has many ways of decrypting an encrypted message using well developed cryptanalysis algorithms. The overall one-size-fits-all approach is breaking the stream or block cipher as a system of multivariate polynomial equations using a GF(2) binary field. The unknowns in the equations are what we need to solve for as they are the keys. If it is solved the key is recovered.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=V. Bard |first=Gregory |title=Algebraic Cryptanalysis |date=14 August 2009 |publisher=[[Springer New York]] |year=2009 |isbn=978-0-387-88757-9 |edition=1st}}</ref>

[[File:Overview of LILI-128 keystream generators.png|thumb|Overview of LILI-128 keystream generators]]
One of the approaches to achieve this is the attack on stream cipher done with the help of an over defined system of algebraic equations. Thus the <math>2^{92}</math> toyocrypt (TOYOCRYPT-HRI) stream cipher<ref>Mihaljević, M.J., & Imai, H. (2002). Cryptanalysis of TOYOCRYPT-HS1 Stream Cipher. ''IEICE Trans. Fundam. Electron. Commun. Comput. Sci., 85-A'', 66-73.</ref> can be attacked in <math>2^{49}</math> [[Clock rate|CPU clocks]] with only 20 KB of keystream which is the fastest attack to break this encryption. [[LILI-128]] can be broken with an algebraic attack in <math>2^{57}</math> CPU clocks. If the stream cipher will at most use 10 [[Linear-feedback shift register|Linear Feedback Shift Registers]] (LFSR) and a Boolean function <math>f</math>, the cipher can be broken with a general algebraic attack.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Courtois |first1=Nicolas T. |last2=Meier |first2=Willi |date=2003 |editor-last=Biham |editor-first=Eli |chapter=Algebraic Attacks on Stream Ciphers with Linear Feedback |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |volume=2656 |title=Advances in Cryptology — EUROCRYPT 2003 |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/3-540-39200-9_21?error=cookies_not_supported&code=3636a64e-3f3f-47f6-a82e-4143e21bb090 |language=en |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |publisher=Springer |pages=345–359 |doi=10.1007/3-540-39200-9_21 |isbn=978-3-540-39200-2|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref>

If the cipher is having non linear equation system the attacker can try to replace the non linear terms with variables thus exceeding the variable count than in the original non linear equation. If the new equation system is solvable, they put the variable solution thus making the original equation linear. Common algebraic equation can be used then to solve the system.

To make good approximation for the key value pairs in the cipher sent using [[linear cryptanalysis]] is another method of solving the cipher. One can use <math>2^{21}</math> known plaintexts to break the 8 round [[Data Encryption Standard]] (DES) and <math>2^{47}</math> plaintexts to break the 16 round DES in this method which is also one of the first practically described use case of algebraic attack using linear cryptanalysis.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Matsui |first=Mitsuru |date=1994 |editor-last=Helleseth |editor-first=Tor |chapter=Linear Cryptanalysis Method for DES Cipher |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |volume=765 |title=Advances in Cryptology — EUROCRYPT '93 |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/3-540-48285-7_33?error=cookies_not_supported&code=41c26bbc-1289-4840-9470-ca3f8479c2e2 |language=en |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |publisher=Springer |pages=386–397 |doi=10.1007/3-540-48285-7_33 |isbn=978-3-540-48285-7|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref>

[[Cube attack|Cube attacks]] later developed are one of the algebraic attack sub method by which the [[Bluetooth]] E0 encryption can be converted into the plaintext in fraction of a second. This was further improvement from the precomputation algorithms that were the fastest known to break the Bluetooth cipher.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Armknecht |first=Frederik |date=2004 |editor-last=Roy |editor-first=Bimal |chapter=Improving Fast Algebraic Attacks |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |volume=3017 |editor2-last=Meier |editor2-first=Willi |title=Fast Software Encryption |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-25937-4_5?error=cookies_not_supported&code=40de3ff3-c3e9-4053-bb86-aa96de573f32 |language=en |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |publisher=Springer |pages=65–82 |doi=10.1007/978-3-540-25937-4_5 |isbn=978-3-540-25937-4|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref>

=== Modern algorithms ===
SAT solvers are widely used standard of doing algebraic attacks.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Li |first1=Zhengyu |last2=Bright |first2=Curtis |last3=Ganesh |first3=Vijay |date=2024-03-24 |title=A SAT Solver and Computer Algebra Attack on the Minimum Kochen-Specker Problem (Student Abstract) |url=https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/30472 |journal=Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence |language=en |volume=38 |issue=21 |pages=23559–23560 |doi=10.1609/aaai.v38i21.30472 |issn=2374-3468|doi-access=free }}</ref> It is similar to how we solve NP-complete problems which are the hardest problems to solve in the NP class and easy to verify in polynomial time. SAT solvers take up the logical formula and return the Boolean true or false value depending on whether the solution exists for the problem or not.

Gröbner basis attack uses [[Gröbner basis|Gröbner basis of an ideal]] which is a polynomial equation system with same variety (or solutions) and is easier to solve but computationally expensive. The reduced Gröbner basis generating the zero dimensional ideal has a univariate form and can be solved with factorization. On a 3 round pure cipher, a 96 bit key is found under a second and uses very less (plaintext, ciphertext) pairs. Thus this is a lot faster than using exhaustive search of key space using Gröbner basis.<ref>{{Citation |last1=Buchmann |first1=Johannes |title=Block ciphers sensitive to Groebner Basis Attacks |date=2005 |url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2005/200 |access-date=2026-05-20 |id=2005/200 |last2=Pychkine |first2=Andrei |last3=Weinmann |first3=Ralf-Philipp}}</ref> This algorithm is directly based from [[Bruno Buchberger]] as he had computed the Gröbner basis of an ideal.<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Daumen |first=Baptiste |title=Practical Study on Solving Polynomial Systems corresponding to Algebraic Attacks on Symmetric Primitives |date=2025-09-08 |degree=other |publisher=Master Parisien de Recherche en Informatique (MPRI), École Polytechnique |url=https://inria.hal.science/hal-05468019 |language=en}}</ref>

=== Preventive techniques ===
There has been research work for strengthening the [[Crypto-1]] stream cipher by causing the attackers to use too high CPU time and too high memory in the modified version of Crypto-1. This is one of the demonstrated ways to protect encryption from algebraic attack in RFID systems.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=School of Computing, Telkom University, Indonesia |last2=Afianti |first2=Farah |last3=Barmawi |first3=Ari M. |last4=School of Computing, Telkom University, Indonesia |date=June 2015 |title=Strengthening Crypto-1 Cipher Against Algebraic Attacks |url=http://journals.itb.ac.id/index.php/jictra/article/view/1193 |journal=Journal of ICT Research and Applications |volume=9 |issue=1 |pages=88–109 |doi=10.5614/itbj.ict.res.appl.2015.9.1.5|doi-access=free }}</ref>

[[S-box]] technique<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Abbasi |first1=Aqsa Zafar |last2=Rafiq |first2=Ayesha |last3=Jaghdam |first3=Ines Hilali |last4=Maatki |first4=Chemseddine |last5=Hassen |first5=Walid |last6=Alshammari |first6=Badr M. |date=2025-11-04 |title=Generalized triangle group based S-box construction for secure image encryption |journal=Scientific Reports |language=en |volume=15 |issue=1 |pages=38608 |doi=10.1038/s41598-025-22558-2  |doi-access=free|issn=2045-2322 |pmc=12586604 |pmid=41188397}}</ref> is used for securing image transfer so that the information enclosed within the image cannot be decrypted.<ref name=":1" /> It has thus been used in satellite image encryption using [[Fredkin gate|Fredkin logic]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Alexan |first1=Wassim |last2=Maher |first2=Engy Aly |last3=Mamdouh |first3=Eyad |last4=Youssef |first4=Mohamed |last5=Ehab |first5=Noha |date=2025-10-27 |title=A chaos-based augmented image encryption scheme for satellite images using Fredkin logic |journal=Scientific Reports |language=en |volume=15 |issue=1 |pages=37345 |doi=10.1038/s41598-025-22008-z  |doi-access=free|issn=2045-2322 |pmc=12559233 |pmid=41145567 |bibcode=2025NatSR..1537345A }}</ref>

== Notable examples ==
[[KeeLoq|Keeloq]] remote access to car and door alarms with an experimental attack was successfully broken in 2007. Given <math>2^{16}</math> known plaintexts, a [[Slide attack|slide]]-algebraic attack that uses a SAT solver can break <math>2^{53}</math> Keeloq encryptions in <math>2^{64}</math> CPU clocks. It is also the first time that a real life full round cipher has been broken using an algebraic attack.<ref>{{Citation |last1=Courtois |first1=Nicolas T. |title=Algebraic and Slide Attacks on KeeLoq |date=2007 |url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2007/062 |access-date=2026-05-20 |id=2007/062 |last2=Bard |first2=Gregory V. |last3=Wagner |first3=David}}</ref>

Bluetooth stream cipher E0 is decoded easily by many attacks including algebraic and hence are removed from 4.0 versions which used the [[AES-CCMP|AES-CCM]] encryption standard. For E0's four LFSR system its initial value can be found using an algebraic attack that has a realistic space complexity of <math>2^{83}</math> (84MB [[Random-access memory|RAM]]) and time complexity of <math>2^{87}</math> CPU clocks.<ref>{{Citation |last1=Shaked |first1=Yaniv |title=Cryptanalysis of the Bluetooth E0 Cipher using OBDD's |date=2006 |url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2006/072 |access-date=2026-05-20 |id=2006/072 |last2=Wool |first2=Avishai}}</ref>

Data Encryption Standard (DES) although robust from complete break was last widely used in 2001 for banking services and government websites as a result of vulnerability to algebraic attacks. One of the algebraic attacks on 6 round DES can be done with just a single plaintext.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Courtois |first1=Nicolas T. |last2=Bard |first2=Gregory V. |date=2007 |editor-last=Galbraith |editor-first=Steven D. |chapter=Algebraic Cryptanalysis of the Data Encryption Standard |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |volume=4887 |title=Cryptography and Coding |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-77272-9_10?error=cookies_not_supported&code=1c8a65eb-bb6a-414a-88da-d071ad8393de |language=en |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |publisher=Springer |pages=152–169 |doi=10.1007/978-3-540-77272-9_10 |isbn=978-3-540-77272-9 |doi-access=|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Reduced round version of [[Data Encryption Standard]] (DES) and KeeLoq remote car locking ciphers were broken by [[SAT solver|SAT solvers]] which outperformed the [[Gröbner basis]] technique which is used when the keystream is extremely small. It was shown that the Hitag2 ciphers commonly used in automobiles can be broken in few hours using the same SAT solvers and algebraic attack with conversion.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Courtois |first1=Nicolas T. |last2=O’Neil |first2=Sean |last3=Quisquater |first3=Jean-Jacques |date=2009 |editor-last=Samarati |editor-first=Pierangela |chapter=Practical Algebraic Attacks on the Hitag2 Stream Cipher |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |volume=5735 |editor2-last=Yung |editor2-first=Moti |editor3-last=Martinelli |editor3-first=Fabio |editor4-last=Ardagna |editor4-first=Claudio A. |title=Information Security |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-642-04474-8_14?error=cookies_not_supported&code=b0a9bd76-a933-4ea3-89a5-c249d76aec7b |language=en |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |publisher=Springer |pages=167–176 |doi=10.1007/978-3-642-04474-8_14 |isbn=978-3-642-04474-8|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Modern cryptography algorithms such as [[Post-quantum cryptography|Post Quantum Cryptography]] are trying to prevent algebraic attacks made by hackers using quantum computer in future. One such algorithm is Cryptographic Suite for Crystal Lattices (CRYSTALS). <ref>{{Cite web |title=Post-quantum Cryptography |url=https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/project/post-quantum-cryptography/ |access-date=2026-05-19 |website=Microsoft Research |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Schwabe |first=Peter |title=CRYSTALS |url=https://pq-crystals.org/index.shtml |access-date=2026-05-20 |website=pq-crystals.org}}</ref>
